ideas: Who the colleague is and what makes them difficult
A specific situation that caused tension
What you did and how things are now

phrases.meaning: claim praise for someone else's work

phrases.phrase: give someone the benefit of the doubt

phrases.meaning: how colleagues deal with each other

model: I'd like to talk about a colleague called Tuan, who joined my team about a year ago. He's very clever and hard-working, but from the start he rubbed a lot of people the wrong way. He tended to interrupt in meetings, and a few times he took credit for ideas that other people had suggested, including one of mine. The worst moment was when we presented a report to our director, and Tuan talked as if he'd done the analysis alone, even though I'd been working on it for three weeks. I was really annoyed, but I managed to keep my cool during the meeting. Afterwards, I decided to have a quiet word with him instead of complaining to our manager. I tried to give him the benefit of the doubt, and it turned out he genuinely hadn't realised how it sounded. He's only recently moved from a company where people worked much more individually. Since then, I've tried to set clear boundaries, for example by agreeing at the start who'll present which part of a project. I've also made an effort to include him in lunch and small talk, because I think a lot of tension comes from not knowing each other. Honestly, we've built a decent working relationship now. We'll never be best friends, but we get on well with each other, and I've learned that a calm, private conversation usually works better than a big confrontation.
